extracted.intended_audience: media professionals and credentialed reporters who cover the NBA (and NBA communications/operations staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Official NBA media guide pages for referee/officiating operations containing media contacts, registration/access instructions, seasonal key dates and deadlines, standardized officiating materials (hand signals, court diagram, video rulebook), and metrics of officiating experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media Central access & registration
rubrics_metrics.description: The Media Central Web site (https://mediacentral.nba.com) is a password-protected site designed for media who regularly cover the NBA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Membership to the site includes easy access to box scores and statistics, team game notes, press releases, NBA News archives, credential applications, team logos, head shots of players and league executives, and information about the WNBA and NBA D-League. The site is updated continuously. To register for the site please visit https://mediacentral.nba.com/register/.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Basketball Communications contacts
rubrics_metrics.description: A listed set of media contacts (names, titles, phone numbers, emails) for Basketball Communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media should contact the named communications staff (e.g., Tim Frank, Maureen Coyle, Mark Broussard, Peter Lagiovane) for press-relations inquiries; phone numbers and emails are provided for direct outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Rulebook content coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The NBA Video Rulebook Web site (http://www.nba.com/videorulebook/) illustrates fouls and violations with real, in-game video clips to test knowledge of and learn more about NBA game rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Web site currently features more than 100 videos and accompanying descriptions and will be continually updated. Videos and descriptions include blocks and charges (including collisions, restricted area positioning), fouls and violations of post play, illegal screen/pick techniques, flagrant fouls (1 and 2) and explanations, traveling and dribbling violations, free-throw violations, technical fouls, instant replay examples, and miscellaneous violations (timeouts, inbounds fouls, hand checking, fouls away from play).

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Rulebook precedence (Video Rulebook disclaimer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that the video Web site is not a substitute for the Official NBA Rulebook, which takes precedence over any discrepancies written on the site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When there is any discrepancy between the Video Rulebook content and the Official NBA Rulebook, the Official NBA Rulebook controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referee hand signals (standardized signals)
rubrics_metrics.description: Referee Hand Signals section — standardized hand signals are documented for on-court officiating communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials are expected to use the standard set of hand signals as illustrated in the guide (visuals/examples provided on the Hand Signals pages) to communicate calls clearly to players, coaches, and spectators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official court dimensions and markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Official NBA Court Diagram and marking specifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key specification: 'ALL LINES SHALL BE 2 IN. WIDE (NEUTRAL ZONES EXCLUDED).' The diagram also indicates standard distances and zone measurements used on an official NBA court (examples shown on the diagram: 16 FT (outside), 12 FT (outside), 50 FT (inside), 72 IN., 4 FT., and other court-specific dimension callouts). Use the official diagram for precise placement and measurement of lines/areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: First allowable reporting date for players in preseason NBA Global Games
rubrics_metrics.description: First allowable date for players participating in preseason NBA Global Games to report to their teams (no earlier than 11 a.m. local time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Players participating in preseason Global Games may not report to their teams before this stated allowable date and time; local time restriction applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training camps open for teams in preseason NBA Global Games
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Camps open for all teams participating in preseason NBA Global Games.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams participating in Global Games may open training camps on the listed date for those teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: First allowable reporting date for all other players
rubrics_metrics.description: First allowable date for all other players to report to their teams (no earlier than 11 a.m. local time).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-Global-Games players have a separate earliest reporting date and the same 11 a.m. local time restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training camps open for all other teams
rubrics_metrics.description: Training Camps open for all other teams (i.e., teams not participating in preseason Global Games).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These teams may open training camps on the specified date for those teams.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA preseason end / rosters set for Opening Day
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Preseason ends and rosters set for NBA Opening Day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the preseason end date, rosters are finalized for Opening Day as indicated in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of NBA Regular Season (Tip-Off)
rubrics_metrics.description: Start of the NBA Regular Season (NBA Tip-Off 2016 noted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide lists the official season start date for scheduling and media planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: 10-day contracts signing window opens
rubrics_metrics.description: 10-day contracts may now be signed (date listed in the Key Dates section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams become eligible to sign 10-day contracts beginning on this date; contractual timing rules apply per Collective Bargaining Agreement and league policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee date for contracts (season guarantees take effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: All contracts are guaranteed for the remainder of the season (date indicated in Key Dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A specified date triggers guarantee provisions for contracts for the remainder of that season; teams and players should consult contract language and league policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Global Games / NBA Canada Series scheduling (event listings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Listings of international preseason and regular-season NBA Global Games and NBA Canada Series matchups and locations (e.g., Golden State Warriors vs. Toronto Raptors — Vancouver; Real Madrid vs. OKC Thunder — Madrid; FC Barcelona vs. OKC Thunder — Barcelona; Houston vs. New Orleans — Shanghai/Beijing; other international matchups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are announced event schedules used for media planning and logistics; details include teams, opponents, and host cities.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA All-Star and Playoffs timeline items
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Dates include NBA All-Star weekend date and the sequence marking regular season end, rosters set for NBA Playoffs (3 p.m. ET), and the begin date for NBA Playoffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates are used for media planning and determine playoff eligibility and scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Early Entry Eligibility Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Early Entry Eligibility Deadline (11:59 p.m. ET).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective early-entry draft entrants must meet this deadline (time zone specified) to be considered for the draft pool.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Draft Early Entry Entrant Withdrawal Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: NBA Draft Early Entry Entrant Withdrawal Deadline (5:00 p.m. ET).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early entrants who wish to withdraw must do so by this date/time to retain NCAA eligibility or to remove themselves from the draft process, per NBA rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portsmouth Invitational Tournament / Draft Combine scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Dates list events such as the Portsmouth Invitational Tournament and the NBA Draft Combine (Chicago) with their scheduled dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These events are part of the pre-draft evaluation calendar and are relevant to media coverage and player evaluation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Playoff Eligibility Waiver Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Playoff Eligibility Waiver Deadline (date listed in Key Dates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams and players must meet waiver/eligibility deadlines by the specified date to be eligible for postseason participation; consult league policy for waiver procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference Semifinals / Conference Finals / NBA Finals scheduling
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Dates include the start of Conference Semifinals, Conference Finals (possible schedule moves noted), and the beginning of the NBA Finals (with latest possible Finals date also listed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provide timeline windows for postseason scheduling; the guide notes possible date adjustments (e.g., Conference Finals may move up to May 14 or 15).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rosters set for NBA Playoffs (time-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rosters set for NBA Playoffs 2017, 3 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teams' playoff rosters are finalized and locked in at the stated time on the listed date; media should use this time for roster announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: NBA Draft Lottery / NBA Draft date listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Key Dates include the NBA Draft Lottery 2017 and the NBA Draft 2017 dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These dates govern draft order determination and the date of the NBA Draft event for media and team planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Officiating experience metrics (Fast Facts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Officiating Fast Facts present metrics used to summarize officials' experience: 'MOST SEASONS OFFICIATED', 'MOST NBA PLAYOFFS EXPERIENCE', 'MOST REGULAR SEASON GAMES OFFICIATED', 'MOST NBA FINALS EXPERIENCE' with numeric totals for named officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guide uses quantitative metrics (number of seasons, playoff games, regular season games, Finals games) as key indicators of officiating seniority and experience; these are presented as authoritative statistics.
